# Template: AI-usage monitoring notice (for a client's acceptable-use policy)

> **Not legal advice.** This is a plain-language starting point. Have the client's counsel review it
> for every jurisdiction where employees work (monitoring and consent rules vary by state and
> country) before it is adopted. Replace everything in [BRACKETS]. Delete this box.

---

## Monitoring of AI-tool usage

**[COMPANY]** provides computers, networks and accounts for business use. To protect confidential
information, [COMPANY] monitors the use of third-party generative-AI services (for example ChatGPT,
Claude, Gemini and Perplexity) on company devices and networks.

**What is monitored.** When you use these services from a company device or network, [COMPANY]'s
security systems inspect the text you submit in order to detect confidential information such as
passwords, access keys, personal data (for example Social Security or payment card numbers) and
documents marked confidential.

**What is kept.** The system keeps a short security record — the time, the device, the AI service,
the type of sensitive data detected and a risk rating. It does **not** keep the text you typed or
the sensitive value itself.

**What is not monitored.** Other websites and services are not inspected by this system. [Add any
other exclusions the client chooses.]

**Who can see it.** Security records are available to [ROLES, e.g. the IT security team and designated
managers] and are used to protect [COMPANY] and to follow up on policy concerns. Records are kept
for [RETENTION PERIOD].

**What this means for you.** Do not enter passwords, keys, customer or employee personal data, or
confidential documents into AI tools unless [COMPANY] has approved that tool for that purpose.
Approved AI tools are listed at [LOCATION].

**This is not a block.** The system alerts the security team; it does not stop or change what you
send. Using these services on company systems means you accept this monitoring.

Questions: [CONTACT]. Last updated: [DATE].
